title: Ang 1: the Mool Mantar
hookLine: the Granth opens with Ik Onkar, the Mool Mantar and the start of the Japji
tomorrow: what does the Japji look like, laid out on the page?

lines: TWO WORDS ON THE FIRST PAGE.
cards: A comment under a video, aimed at people who look like your family. A joke on the bus about somebody's turban. Two instincts show up at once: shrink, or hit back.
The first words of the Granth weren't written for a bus. They describe the One. But two of them, standing side by side on the first page, speak straight to that moment.

teach.h: THE MOOL MANTAR: THE ROOT FORMULA.
teach.b: Ang one opens with the Mool Mantar, the root formula. In the original: ik onkaar, sat naam, kartaa purakh, nirbhau, nirvair, akaal moorat, ajoonee, saibhan, gur prasaad. One.
Whose name is truth. The creator. Without fear.
Self-existent. Known by the Guru's grace.

teach.h: TRUE IN THE BEGINNING, TRUE NOW.
teach.b: Then the Japji begins, with a short salok, in paraphrase: true in the beginning, true through the ages, true now, and true hereafter.

Something to tell someone tonight: of everything the Granth could open with, its first page describes the One as nirbhau and nirvair, without fear and without hate, in the same breath. Now bring it back to the bus.
Fear makes a person shrink. Hate makes a person strike. Some readers hold these two words up as a mirror: the One is afraid of no one and no one's enemy, and a person can lean that way too.
Stand up, and don't go small.

teach.h: STAND UP, AND MAKE NO ENEMY.
teach.b: Speak plainly, and don't make an enemy. One word without the other tips over: fearless with hate turns into a fight, and no hate without courage turns into silence. The first page keeps them together.

how: Sikhs recite the Mool Mantar at the start of the Japji every morning, and it stands at the head of the Guru Granth Sahib on ang 1; shorter forms of it head later sections of the book.

o: the page holding the Granth's table of contents
the first page: the Mool Mantar and the Japji's start
the page that lists the names of all the Gurus

games.q: the root formula — tap the pairs.

s: the Mool Mantar stands at the very start of the Granth
it opens ang 1, before the Japji's first salok.
nirvair means never standing up to anyone
it sits beside nirbhau: without hate, and without fear.
the Mool Mantar names a God who belongs to Sikhs alone
it describes the One, the creator, timeless and unborn, with no group named.

games.q: in the group chat, a classmate posts a cruel joke about your friend's dastar. everyone's watching to see what you'll do. what does the first page point toward?
o: say nothing: nirvair means you never confront anyone.
say plainly it's not okay, and leave his name and insults out of it.
roast him back harder: nirbhau means you show no fear.
games.why: nirbhau and nirvair stand together on ang 1. fearless with hate turns into a fight; no hate without courage turns into silence.

practice: Read or say the Mool Mantar aloud, slowly, once, from a gutka, a screen, or the words you just heard. Then let it narrow to the two words: nirbhau on a breath in, nirvair on a breath out.
If a face from this week comes to mind, someone who scared you or made you angry, let both words meet it.

wordCard.voice: Ang 1. The first page: the Mool Mantar, the root of everything after it, and the start of the Japji. Today's word.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: nirbhau, without fear; nirvair, without hate or enmity: two words side by side in the Mool Mantar.

carryVoice: Your line: where it begins. Without fear and without hate, side by side. See you tomorrow.
